As for how to report the lower MSD capability, several promising options for allowing a UE to signal improved lower MSD performance have been discussed [R4-2306590]. It is also agreed that the MSD mechanisms, orders and values in existing specs shall all be considered as starting point. Considering there are many MSD mechanisms and the order of aggressor could be up to 9 in existing specs, if UE need to signal all improved MSD information, the signaling overhead might be quite large. One approach with signaling the essential information as well as the idea to reduce signaling overhead is network can require UE only to report the top K largest MSD values together with its mechanism indexing and improved MSD values. For example K = 1, If K=1, Network scheduling with reference on top largest value of reported lower MSD Figure 7.1.3.2-1 Example illustration of network query on low-MSD information, K=1 If K=2, Network scheduling with reference on top two largest value of reported lower MSD Figure 7.1.3.2-2 Example illustration of network query on low-MSD information, K=2 Or alternative low-MSD signaling expression: If K=1, Network scheduling with reference on top largest value of reported lower MSD Figure 7.1.3.2-3 Example illustration of network query on low-MSD information, K=1 Figure 7.1.3.2-4 Example illustration of network query on low-MSD information, K=2 With such adaptive signalling approach, UE does not need to report all low-MSD information over all supported band combinations. UE may also not need to restore all improved low-MSD points, it only needs to restore top K largest low-MSD information which can save the size of UE memory to smaller one. Network also does not need to restore large amount of low-MSD information that only a few of them are interested band combinations.

{"chunk_id":"R4-2506469-001","collection":"ran4_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["vivo"],"tdocNumber":"R4-2506469","title":"Discussion on RRM performance requirements for beam management and positioning accuracy"},"point_id":"16178656882229171641"}
The RRM core requirements for AI/ML-based beam management were discussed in the past several meetings. According to the working plan, the performance part of this WI will begin to be discussed in this meeting. Therefore, in this paper, we will provide our preliminary analysis on the following aspects: Measurement accuracy requirement RRM test cases Regarding the measurement accuracy, a relatively thorough analysis has already been conducted in the core part section. As for BM-Case 1, the supported reporting content is as follows, mainly including: CRI or SSBRI of beam K Absolute predicted RSRP for Top-1 beam Differential predicted RSRP with reference to the largest predicted RSRP Regarding this prediction accuracy, the corresponding accuracy requirement needs to be defined. Since RAN4 has not previously established similar requirements, the basic framework and conditions for this accuracy requirement need further discussion within RAN4. To some extent, this also depends on the ongoing discussions regarding testability. As for deriving the specific accuracy values, based on our understanding, they should be determined through the simulations currently being conducted. Secondly, for Absolute Predicted RSRP and Differential Predicted RSRP, when the predicted RSRP is required to be reported, its accuracy must be ensured. For Absolute Predicted RSRP, the existing Absolute RSRP accuracy requirements for FR2 can serve as a reference framework for defining this requirement. For Differential Predicted RSRP, similar to the existing Relative RSRP accuracy requirements for FR2, when the UE reports more than one beam, this requirement must also be checked. The specific accuracy values corresponding to these two requirements, as well as the beam prediction accuracy, should be derived from ongoing simulations. Additionally, for performance monitoring, RAN1 has also defined corresponding performance metrics for Top 1 or Top K beam prediction accuracy. From the perspective of UE performance monitoring, the UE shall determine the RS-PAI (Reference Signal Prediction Accuracy Indicator) as the total count of accurate reference signal prediction instances. Accordingly, based on RAN1’s current discussions, the UE needs to report the number of correct predictions out of N inference attempts. Therefore, from a performance standpoint, we believe it is necessary to verify whether the UE correctly reports the number of accurate predictions out of N inference attempts. RAN4 needs to define the requirements for this. Proposal 1: For RRM performance requirements for beam management, RAN4 to consider the following requirements； Absolute Predicted RSRP accuracy Relative Predicted RSRP accuracy Monitoring accuracy for performance accuracy (to verify whether the UE correctly reports the number of accurate predictions out of N inference attempts.)

The WF of last meeting is reproduced as below. Proposals Option 1: allow gNB query UE capability and UE only report certain capability filtered by gNB’s query information. (CMCC, vivo, Skyworks, Meta, OPPO) Option 2: The potential singaling overhead and complexity on lower MSD capability indication shall be carefully considered in RAN4 while the solution details are being worked out (Apple) Option 3: (MTK) To reduce signalling overhead during connection and save UE maximum memory size for storing low-MSD information, an adaptive signalling approach that network can require UE only to report the top K largest MSD values together with its mechanism indexing and improved MSD values is proposed as option 5. Option1 is a popular/ common mechanism which is adopted by many signaling/feature design, we are not against to agree it in RAN4, but we would like to mention RAN2 would enable it even without RAN4 instructing them to do it. Furthermore, it is suggested to discard the complicated mechanism at least in Rel-18.

In the last RAN4 meeting, following options as were listed in WF[3]. Candidate option for signalling overhead reduction Option 1: allow gNB query UE capability and UE only report certain capability filtered by gNB’s query information. (CMCC, vivo, Skyworks, Meta, OPPO) Option 2: The potential singaling overhead and complexity on lower MSD capability indication shall be carefully considered in RAN4 while the solution details are being worked out (Apple) Option 3: (MTK) To reduce signalling overhead during connection and save UE maximum memory size for storing low-MSD information, an adaptive signalling approach that network can require UE only to report the top K largest MSD values together with its mechanism indexing and improved MSD values is proposed as option 5. UE is also allowed to report top K’ largest low-MSD information where K’<K. For the low-MSD terms that are not responded, the MSD in existing specs applies. Option 4: For the sake of signalling overhead reduction, further study if the victim band for a given band combination can be omitted from reporting at least for some of the MSD types (Huawei) To reduce the signalling overhead, it is important point which MSD type is easier to achieve the system benefits and improved system capacity by gNB scheduling aspect. But it is quite difficult to decide the priority of the among MSD information. Hence, we prefer to allow gNB query UE capability and UE only report the certain filtered capability signalling to reduce the signalling overhead. Also, RAN4 can merge the MSD values according to harmonic/harmonic mixing/cross band isolation/ IMD 2/3/4/5 when the UE supports the same MSD values among these MSD types to reduce signalling overhead. Therefore, we propose as follow Proposal #4: RAN4 can allow gNB query UE capability signalling and UE only reported the filtered capability signalling to reduce the signalling overhead. Also can merge MSD types with the same MSD values.
